## Goal

Confirm on the live proxy that the restored liveness-based prefill lease
extension (LP-0MUXQ5QL40027VZ4) stops the kill/retry loop for long local
prefills.

## Context

Fix landed in commit 2ced52ac: `_extend_lease_during_prefill` now extends the
lease on numeric progress advance OR observed slot liveness
(`is_processing`), with the `local_dispatch_max_prefill_seconds` ceiling still
bounding a wedge. Before the fix, `lease_extended_during_prefill` was 0 and
every local prefill >180s was released and cancelled by the no-progress
watchdog, so clients retried into full re-prefills (see LP-0MUXQ5QL40027VZ4).

## Acceptance criteria

1. Over a post-deploy window, `lease_extended_during_prefill` events appear in
   `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log` with `progress=None alive=True` (the b8782
   liveness-only shape), where the pre-fix count was 0.
2. `lease_released ... reason=no_progress_watchdog` count drops sharply versus
   the same-length pre-fix window; `dispatch_first_byte_timeout` and
   `backend_retry ... ReadTimeout` counts drop.
3. Local prefills longer than `local_dispatch_no_progress_timeout_seconds`
   (180s) complete rather than being re-queued repeatedly.
4. A genuinely wedged slot (no progress, no liveness) is still released
   (watchdog reason still fires when appropriate).
5. If (1)-(4) do not hold, roll back commit 2ced52ac from `dev` and record the
   observed evidence.
data.title: Verify liveness-based prefill lease extension on a live post-deploy window

data.description:
## Problem statement

The proxy's author system prompt (`proxy/prompts/author.txt`) sets the content guidelines for all wiki authoring done through the `author` model. It enforces terminology precision (open source vs open weights vs closed), quality standards, and structural rules, but it has no rule requiring project names and recognised domain concepts to be explained when first used.

As a result, LLM-authored wiki pages introduce unfamiliar projects, tools, frameworks, and domain concepts by bare name, leaving readers who lack the background unable to follow the page.

## Users

- **Wiki reader (no deep domain background):** *As a reader without prior exposure to a project or concept, I want unfamiliar names explained in one or two sentences on first mention, so I can follow a page without external research.*
- **Wiki maintainer:** *As a maintainer, I want the author prompt to enforce first-mention explanations, so pages do not need retrospective glossary clean-up.*
- **Proxy operator:** *As the operator, I want the prompt addition to be concise and regression-tested, so it stays within the 64 KB prompt-file limit and cannot silently disappear.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `proxy/prompts/author.txt` contains an explicit rule requiring non-household project/concept names to be explained in one or two sentences on first mention
- [ ] The rule requires acronyms and domain-specific terms to be expanded on first mention
- [ ] The rule excludes widely known terms (e.g. Python, Google) from the requirement
- [ ] The rule states the explanation is inline at first mention and not repeated on later mentions
- [ ] A test asserts the rule text is present in `proxy/prompts/author.txt` (or the prompt-file validation assumes/checks it) so it cannot silently regress
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the change, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs entries
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes

## Constraints

- Keep the addition concise — `author.txt` is loaded on every author request and must stay within the 64 KB prompt-file limit (`MAX_PROMPT_SIZE` in `proxy/proxy/prompt_resolver.py`).
- Match the existing heading and bullet style of `author.txt`.
- Place the rule in the existing "Quality Standards" section, or as a new numbered guideline alongside "Terminology & Precision".

## Existing state

- `proxy/prompts/author.txt` (7.4 KB) has six top-level sections: 1. Terminology & Precision, 2. Wiki Schema & Ownership, 3. Quality Standards, 4. Structural Rules, 5. TTS Audio Generation, 6. What Not To Do. Section 3 has a bulleted list of quality rules; none addresses first-mention name introduction.
- The prompt is auto-loaded per the `author` model entry in `proxy/config.yaml` and resolved by `proxy/proxy/prompt_resolver.py` (`system_prompt.mode` + `.file`; see `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` § Custom system prompts per model / alias).
- Existing prompt tests (`proxy/tests/test_prompt_resolution.py`) validate resolution, mode, and size limits — they do not assert the content of `author.txt`.

## Desired change

Add a "Name Introduction" guideline to `proxy/prompts/author.txt`, requiring that:

- On **first mention in a page**, every project, product, tool, framework, and organisation name is explained in one or two sentences that state what it is and what it does.
- On first mention, every acronym and domain-specific term is expanded and briefly defined.
- Widely known terms (e.g. Python, Google) may be used without explanation.
- The explanation appears inline at the point of first mention, not in a separate glossary section.
- Later mentions of the same name do not repeat the explanation.

Place the rule in the existing "Quality Standards" section (or as a new numbered guideline alongside "Terminology & Precision").

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — prompt bloat:** every author request loads `author.txt`; the added rule must be concise. Mitigation: the file is ~7.4 KB against a 64 KB limit, so the margin is large; keep the rule to a short bullet set.
- **Risk — "widely known" is subjective:** without examples, authors may over- or under-explain. Mitigation: name representative household terms (e.g. Python, Google) in the rule.
- **Risk — silent regression:** prompt files are not currently content-asserted by tests. Mitigation: add a test asserting the rule text is present.
- **Risk — scope creep:** related prompt surfaces (podcast script, research pipeline) live in the separate `open_source_llm` repo. Mitigation: this item changes only `proxy/prompts/author.txt`; record the sibling prompts as linked work, not scope.
- **Assumption:** the rule belongs in `author.txt` (the auto-loaded author system prompt) rather than in a per-page template or post-processing step.
- **Assumption:** unit-testing prompt content is the accepted regression guard; no prompt linting framework is required.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/prompts/author.txt` — Add the "Name Introduction" guideline (Quality Standards section or new numbered guideline).
- `proxy/tests/test_prompt_resolution.py` — Add a content assertion that the rule text is present, guarding against silent regression; reuse the existing prompt-file fixtures/loading helpers.
- `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` — Confirm the custom-prompt documentation still accurately describes `author.txt` after the change; update if the rule changes the described behaviour.

## Related work

- **Origin:** `OSL-0MUV3H9EG0060G50` in the `open_source_llm` worklog — "Project and concept names need to be explained".
- **Sibling work:** the same rule is being added to the in-repo podcast and synthesis generation prompts in `open_source_llm` (`.pi/skills/wiki-podcast-script/scripts/podcast_script.py`, `.pi/skills/research/scripts/research_pipeline.py`).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** No clarifying questions were asked. — **Answer (author):** The seed context (originating item `OSL-0MUV3H9EG0060G50`, exact deliverable, placement guidance, and constraints) was sufficient to draft a complete brief; repo inspection confirmed the current `author.txt` structure and the absence of any content assertions in `proxy/tests/test_prompt_resolution.py`. Source: seed description + repo inspection.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MRWVPDEO009FR63** – Fix slot_benchmark request deduplication and make prompts unique (completed)
- **LP-0MRY4HUSG0037EWA** – [test-failure] test_config_qwen3_next_llama_model_is_qwen3 — failing test (completed)
- **LP-0MSXZ06M5007CPN6** – [MEDIUM] /home/rgardler/projects/llm/proxy/scripts/llama-proxy-logrotate:10 — Expected a statement (invalid-syntax) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: acceptance, accepted, accurately, add, added (+226 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: acceptance, accepted, accurately, add, added (+226 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_think.txt` — matched: acceptance, accepted, accurately, add, added (+226 more)

# Raise Qwen3 cache-ram to 40,960 MiB

Follow-up to LP-0MUPQIEK10079EAW (which verified the 32,768 MiB cap on the
live post-deploy window) and LP-0MUYFC3C5004TCYN.

## Context

The 2026-10-12 post-32-GiB verification
(`docs/dev/prompt-cache-post-deploy-2026-10-12.json`) showed the cache is
still saturating under the current single-slot load:

- 18 evictions over ~4.7 d (1.28% of requests; 65 -> 18 vs the length-matched
  8 GiB window, a 72.9%/req reduction);
- 26.3% of cache-state samples above 90% of the 32,768 MiB cap (vs 22.0% at
  8 GiB);
- observed maximum 16 concurrently-retained prompts, cache peak 32,765.6 MiB
  (fully saturated).

`scripts/prompt_cache_analysis.py --recommend` over that measurement derives
**40,960 MiB (40 GiB)**:

    per-prompt state 2,013 MiB x observed max 16 x 1.25 margin = 40,260 MiB
    -> round up to 40,960 MiB (holds ~20 prompts >= observed 16)

Headroom is safe (host available 79,248 MiB - 40,960 = 38,288 MiB, well above
the 12,743.7 MiB reserve = max(8 GiB, 10% MemTotal)), so the
`server_prompt_cache::alloc()` OOM fallback (`limit_size = 0.4 * size()`) is
not approached.

## Goal

As a proxy operator, raise the Qwen3 prompt-cache cap to the derived
40,960 MiB so the cache stops saturating and evicting session prefixes under
the single-slot load, with the derivation and headroom recorded.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `models.ini` `[Qwen3]` `cache-ram` raised 32768 -> 40960, with the
   derivation (per-prompt 2,013 MiB x observed max 16 x 1.25) and the
   2026-10-12 measurement reference recorded in the comment block.
2. Headroom invariant re-checked at 40,960 MiB: MemAvailable - 40960 >= reserve
   (reserve = max(8 GiB, 10% MemTotal)); the OOM fallback path is documented
   as avoided.
3. Deploy via `/skill:start-proxy --restart` (never kill the proxy manually);
   confirm the spawned Qwen3 child carries `--cache-ram 40960` (and
   `--ctx-checkpoints 32`, no `--swa-full`).
4. `docs/dev/prompt-cache-tuning.md` updated with the new cap, the derivation
   and the deploy evidence.
5. Full project test suite passes.

## Non-goals

- Changing `ctx-checkpoints` / `checkpoint-every-n-tokens` (kept at 32; the
  checkpoint term is not the lever, see `docs/dev/prompt-cache-tuning.md`).
- Re-tuning routing cold/warm thresholds.
- The live post-deploy validation of this change (separate follow-up).

Discovered from: LP-0MUPQIEK10079EAW
data.title: Raise Qwen3 cache-ram to 40,960 MiB

# Validate the 40,960 MiB cache-ram change on a live post-deploy window

Follow-up to the "Raise Qwen3 cache-ram to 40,960 MiB" item and to
LP-0MUPQIEK10079EAW.

## Goal

After the 40,960 MiB cap has been deployed and a comparable post-deploy window
has been gathered, empirically confirm a positive impact versus the 32,768 MiB
window: evictions continue to fall (ideally to ~0) with no throughput or
client-visible first-byte latency regression.

## Blocked by

The raise item — this validation must not start until 40,960 MiB is live.
Waiting for the post-deploy window is expected (the 2026-10-12 verification
used ~4.7 d / 1,404 requests).

## Acceptance criteria

1. Confirm the spawned Qwen3 child llama-server args include
   `--cache-ram 40960` and `--ctx-checkpoints 32`, and no `--swa-full`.
2. Capture a post-deploy measurement with
   `scripts/prompt_cache_analysis.py --json --recommend --cache-ram-filter 40960`
   over a window comparable to the 32 GiB verification window (~4.7 d /
   1,404 requests) or longer, saved as a committed artifact.
3. Evictions fall further versus the 32,768 MiB window (18 -> fewer),
   `tokens_prefilled`/req and forced full-prefills do not rise, and held
   prompts do not fall.
4. `prompt_eval_tok_s`, `decode_tok_s` and `first_byte_ms` (proxy-side) do not
   regress versus the 32,768 MiB measurement.
5. Record the before/after figures on this item and on LP-0MUPQIEK10079EAW,
   and update `docs/dev/prompt-cache-tuning.md`.

## Notes

- Control for the slot profile (the 3 -> 1 slot change, LP-0MU1S617L) and for
  window length; the 2026-10-12 verification found throughput/wall metrics
  confounded by those.
- Proxy logs rotate quickly; capture `first_byte_ms` over an aligned proxy
  glob at measurement time.
- If the cache still saturates at 40,960 MiB, record the new `--recommend`
  output rather than raising again in this item.

Discovered from: LP-0MUPQIEK10079EAW
